response.internal_assessment: I have one month. That's it. $2,400 in savings and $263 left over each month if nothing changes — but that's barely anything, one bad week and I'm behind on rent. I'm not panicking but I'm not stupid either. This job pays the bills just barely, and I have zero attachment to it. I need more income coming in, or I need my expenses down, or both. Probably both. The car wash isn't going anywhere but I need something on top of it. I've got time on evenings and weekends. I need to use them.

chosen_actions.description: Search for a second part-time or gig-based income source — delivery driving (DoorDash, Instacart), warehouse shifts, or weekend labor gigs. Target something flexible that doesn't conflict with car wash hours.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: time (evenings and weekends), phone for app signup
chosen_actions.reasoning: I have manual labor skills and customer service experience. Gig work requires no resume, no interview, no waiting — I can sign up tonight and be earning within a week. Even $400-600/month extra buys me serious breathing room and pushes L0 threat way down. This is the highest-leverage move I can make right now.

chosen_actions.description: Post on Craigslist and ask around about finding a roommate to split rent, or look into whether a cheaper place exists nearby. Current living situation is a solo arrangement — cutting housing cost by $300-400/month would be significant.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: time to post listings, small effort
chosen_actions.reasoning: Housing is almost certainly my biggest expense. If I can bring in a roommate or move somewhere cheaper, the monthly surplus goes from marginal to manageable. Low attachment to current place, no lease complications I can't navigate. This is slower than gig work but addresses the structural problem.

chosen_actions.description: Go through last month's spending and cut anything non-essential — subscriptions, eating out, anything discretionary. Target cutting $100-150/month from current $2,137 expense load.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: one hour of time, bank account review
chosen_actions.reasoning: I need to know exactly where the $2,137 is going. There's almost certainly some fat to cut. It won't solve the problem alone but it's free money — takes an hour and could buy me another couple weeks of runway while I get the gig work set up.

response.emotional_state: Flat. Focused. Not scared, not hopeful — just pragmatic. The math is what it is. I've been broke before and I know what broke feels like, and I know the difference between broke-with-a-plan and broke-panicking. I'm doing the plan.
response.archetype_self_assessment: Pragmatic Survivor. I don't romanticize this job or this situation. I'm 23, no kids, no anchor, no reason to be precious about any of it. I'll pick up DoorDash shifts and split rent with a stranger if that's what keeps the lights on. Pride is expensive and I can't afford it right now.
response.inner_monologue: Okay. One month. So what. I've got two hands and a phone and I'm not dumb. Sign up for the gig apps tonight — Instacart, DoorDash, maybe Uber if the car passes. Post about the roommate thing tomorrow. Cut the gym membership, cut whatever streaming I'm paying for that I don't need, pack lunch instead of buying it. None of this is complicated. It's just work. The car wash is 8 to 5, that leaves evenings. Use them. Stop sitting on this.
